_comment: Fixture set for the deep-scan cost measurement (docs/PR-PLAN.md, PR 0.6).
Each entry is one run. `group` drives the breakdown in the report; `why`
records what the fixture is there to prove, so a future reader can tell a
deliberate choice from an arbitrary one.
Order matters in exactly one place: the `cache-hit` fixture must come
after the run it repeats, because llm_cache.py means a repeated target
measures a cache hit rather than a scan. That is measured on purpose —
'repeat scans cost near zero' is a marketing claim and should be
evidenced, not asserted — but it must not be mistaken for a fresh scan,
which is why every other fixture is distinct.

deep.why: Small single-purpose library — the floor of the cost range.
Small, few files, no framework.
Small middleware with real request handling.
Small but widely depended on; typical of a transitive dependency.
Near-minimal repo — establishes the fixed overhead per run.
Mid-size app with a Dockerfile — exercises the Docker path alongside code.
Mid-size Express app; representative of a customer's product repo.
Many small Compose stacks — many files, little code per file.
Dockerfile-heavy repository with almost no application code.
Official image source — shell and Dockerfiles rather than an app.
Very large Go repo — should prove the 60-file cap binds.
Very large mixed-language repo.
Very large TypeScript repo — the language the scanner knows best.
Large JS repo with heavy build tooling.
Very large repo in a language with few OWASP patterns — checks that cost is bounded by the cap, not by findings.
Very large standard library.
The largest realistic input. If cost is flat here, it is flat everywhere.
Fills all 10 code-finding prompt slots — measures worst-case token cost, which clean repos understate.
Classic vulnerable PHP app — worst case in a second language.
OWASP Top 10 by construction — worst case for the prompt builder.
Common base image with a long CVE list — exercises Trivy at volume.
Slim image — fewer CVEs, shows the spread across image sizes.
Alpine base — different package ecosystem for Trivy.
Bundled synthetic logs — the deterministic baseline for the log path.
System logs, falling back to synthetic on a container without readable log files. Recorded either way; `used_fallback` says which.
Our own repo. PRIVATE — if GIT_TOKEN's scope excludes private repo read this returns 404 or a rate limit rather than results, which is itself worth knowing.
Anthony's second repository.
Deliberate repeat of vuln-juice-shop. Measures the cache-hit cost, not a scan — must run after it.

surface.why: Self-scan. The release gate is grade A (PRD §7), so the grade is recorded as well as the timing.
